situation: On Monday morning, Garoua is cloudy and it rains, so Idrissa carries an umbrella. His cousin in Paris says on the phone: "But Garoua has a hot climate, so why do you need an umbrella?"
Idrissa does not know how to explain the difference between the rain of today and the hot climate of Garoua.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Idrissa cannot explain the difference between today's rain and the hot climate of Garoua.
What are the conditions in Garoua on Monday morning?
On Monday morning, Garoua is cloudy and it rains.
How can Idrissa explain the difference to his cousin?
He can say that rain today is the weather, while the climate is the usual pattern of Garoua over many years.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to distinguish weather from climate, and to know how weather elements are measured.

qa.q: The condition of the air at a place today, for example cloudy and rainy, is called ______. What is the missing word?
qa.a: It is called weather. Weather changes from hour to hour and from day to day.

qa.q: The average weather of a place over about 30 years is called ______. What is the missing word?
qa.a: It is called climate. For example, Garoua has a tropical climate with a wet season and a dry season.

sum.title: I. Definitions
defs: Weather is the condition of the atmosphere at a particular place and time, for example sunny, rainy, hot or windy.
Climate is the average weather condition of a place over a long period, usually 30 years or more.

qa.q: At Garoua airport, there is a place where instruments measure the weather every day. What is it called?
qa.a: It is called a weather station, or meteorological station.

sum.title: II. The Weather Station
defs: A weather station is a place with instruments that measure and record the elements of weather, to study weather and climate and to make forecasts.

qa.q: Look at the diagram. Which instrument measures temperature, and which one measures rainfall?
qa.a: The thermometer measures temperature in degrees Celsius. The rain gauge measures rainfall in millimetres.

qa.title: Question 2
qa.q: Which instruments measure wind direction and wind speed?
qa.a: The wind vane shows wind direction. The anemometer measures wind speed in km/h or knots.

qa.q: On a map, a line joins all places with the same temperature. What do we call a line that joins places of equal value?
qa.a: It is called an isoline. A line joining places of equal temperature is an isotherm, and one joining places of equal rainfall is an isohyet.

sum.title: III. Weather Elements, Instruments and Isolines
intro: The main weather elements, their instruments, units and isolines are the following. An isoline is a line joining places of equal value.
items: – Wind direction: wind vane, compass points.
– Wind speed: anemometer, km/h or knots, isotach.
– Cloud cover: observed by eye, oktas (eighths), isoneph.

evaluation: Give one difference between weather and climate.
Weather is the condition of the atmosphere for a short time, while climate is the average weather over about 30 years.
Name the instrument and the unit used to measure atmospheric pressure.
Pressure is measured with a barometer, in millibars.
An isohyet is a line on a map that joins places with the same amount of rainfall.
remediation: The condition of the atmosphere at a given time is ______.
The average weather over 30 years is ______.
Wind speed is measured with an ______.
A line joining places of equal temperature is an ______.
A line joining places of equal pressure is an ______.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. weather 2. climate 3. rain gauge 4. anemometer 5. isotherm 6. isobar
end.homework: Put one bottle of water in the sun and another in the shade for one hour. Touch both and write down which is hotter and why.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 32: Weather Elements — Atmospheric Temperatures.
teacherNote: Weather elements are sometimes classified into measured elements (temperature, rainfall, pressure, wind, humidity, sunshine) and observed elements (cloud cover, visibility).
Cloud cover is measured in oktas (eighths of the sky).
